skill.name: air-quality
skill.description: 環境省の大気汚染物質広域監視システム(AEROS・そらまめくん)から、PM2.5・光化学オキシダントなどの測定値(速報値)を取得する。全国約1,600測定局の最新1時間値・測定局ごとの今日/7日分・都道府県ごとの月次履歴に対応。「今のPM2.5」「空気が悪い?」の質問に答える。APIキー・ログイン不要。確定値(過去の公式統計)は対象外。
skill.summary: Retrieve provisional Japanese air quality measurements, station histories, and PM2.5 advisories from public AEROS endpoints.
skill.author: tahodev

content.value_statement: Japanese air quality measurements are spread across station snapshots, histories, and advisory feeds. This skill retrieves public AEROS data and reports provisional readings with station names and measurement times.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve the latest nationwide hourly CSV using the timestamp published in AEROS metadata.
Filter station readings by name, address, municipality, prefecture code, or exact station code using the Python helper.
Rank matching stations by a selected numeric measurement while placing missing readings last.
Cache hourly CSV downloads locally and support explicit refresh through the Python helper.
Provide documented retrieval workflows for station daily and seven-day CSVs and prefecture monthly API histories.
Provide a documented workflow for reading public PM2.5 advisory areas.
limitations: Coverage is limited to Japanese AEROS stations, and the supplied CSV lacks coordinates for nearest-station searches.
Measurements are provisional, some stations report late, and missing readings cannot be inferred.
The Python helper requires Python 3 and network access; history and advisory retrieval use separate documented endpoints.
The skill does not provide finalized statistics, medical advice, or personal decisions about outdoor activity.

use_cases.title: Review Local Station Readings
use_cases.description: Find recent PM2.5 readings for a municipality and distinguish roadside stations from general ambient monitoring stations.

use_cases.title: Compare Provisional Station Histories
use_cases.description: Retrieve daily, seven-day, or monthly station records for a defined region while preserving missing readings and reporting delays.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Sourced Air Quality Update
use_cases.description: Summarize station measurements and published PM2.5 advisories with timestamps, source references, and clear provisional-data labels.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Municipality
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the latest PM2.5 readings for [municipality]. Include station names, station types, and measurement times in JST.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Prefecture Stations
prompt_templates.prompt: List the five highest measured [pollutant] readings in prefecture [code]. Label provisional values and identify missing readings separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare stations within a prefecture.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Station History
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the last seven days for station [code]. Summarize PM2.5 changes, report missing hours, and preserve measurement timestamps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: inspect a station time series using the documented CSV endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Review Monthly Data and Advisories
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve monthly PM2.5 records for [prefecture code] and [month]. Summarize station coverage, missing data, reporting delays, and current official PM2.5 advisories.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine historical measurements with a separately dated advisory check.

best_practices: Include the station name, station type, measurement time in JST, and provisional-data label with every reported reading.
Use published metadata for the latest hourly URL and verify the CSV header before interpreting a successful HTTP response.
Keep missing readings explicit and narrow historical requests by station, measurement, and period.
anti_patterns: Treating hourly provisional readings as finalized statistics or personal medical guidance.
Replacing missing readings with guessed values or presenting delayed station records as current.
Downloading an entire monthly prefecture dataset when a latest-hour snapshot or daily station CSV meets the request.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The documented AEROS endpoints are public and require no API key, login, or user registration.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The lookup helper requires Python 3, and the documented curl workflows require curl.

faq.question: Does it cover air quality outside Japan?
faq.answer: No. It uses Japan's AEROS monitoring service and its public station measurements.

faq.question: Are the readings finalized or always current?
faq.answer: No. Readings are provisional, and some stations report late. Include each measurement timestamp and use official finalized statistics when required.

faq.question: Where does the helper store downloaded data?
faq.answer: It caches hourly CSV files under ~/.cache/kurashi-skill/air-quality. Matching timestamps reuse the cache unless refresh is requested.

faq.question: Can it decide whether outdoor activity is safe?
faq.answer: No. Personal health decisions are outside scope. Consult published PM2.5 advisories, local authority announcements, and appropriate health guidance.
